articles.headline: El concurso para reparar el puente romano de Lugo queda desierto
articles.subtitle: Ninguna empresa se presentó a la licitación de 70.605 euros para sustituir los sillares dañados por la riada de 2023, y el Concello deberá revisar el pliego o buscar otra vía de contratación.
articles.body:
La licitación que el Ayuntamiento de Lugo abrió hace unas semanas para reparar los daños que la riada de 2023 causó en el puente romano ha quedado desierta. Ninguna empresa presentó oferta para unos trabajos presupuestados en 70.605 euros, IVA incluido. El Concello deberá decidir ahora si revisa las condiciones económicas, convoca un nuevo concurso o recurre a otra fórmula de contratación.

El proyecto preveía retirar las chapas metálicas y los tableros colocados de urgencia tras la crecida y sustituirlos por doce bloques de granito labrados a medida en las pilas 3, 4 y 5. La combinación de un importe ajustado y una exigencia técnica alta —grúas desde la calzada superior, supervisión arqueológica continua y dependencia del caudal del Miño— habría dejado el concurso sin candidatos.

El retraso empuja los trabajos, como mínimo, hacia la primavera o el verano que viene, de modo que el paso seguirá mostrando los parches provisionales mientras lo cruzan caminantes y peregrinos del Camino Primitivo. El gobierno local había previsto iniciar la intervención en los primeros meses de 2027.

No es la primera vez que el viaducto se somete a una obra complicada. Entre 2011 y 2013 se rehabilitó con cargo al 1% Cultural y un presupuesto cercano al millón de euros, en unos trabajos que se retrasaron al aparecer restos arqueológicos en el puente. Desde entonces perdió el tráfico rodado, unos 12.000 vehículos diarios, y quedó reservado a peatones.

articles.headline: La A-54 entre Lugo y Santiago cumple 30 años de obras sin fecha de apertura
articles.subtitle: Los 16 kilómetros entre Melide y Arzúa, último tramo pendiente, acumulan meses de retraso sobre el calendario que el Gobierno manejaba para este otoño.
articles.body:
La autovía A-54, que debe unir Lugo y Santiago a lo largo de algo más de 93 kilómetros, sigue sin fecha de puesta en servicio. El tramo final, los 16 kilómetros entre Melide y Arzúa, acumulaba en agosto ocho meses de retraso sobre un calendario que lo daba por terminado en enero, y el delegado del Gobierno en Galicia llegó a situar la apertura en septiembre u octubre.

El último hito administrativo fue una tercera modificación del contrato de obras aprobada por el Consejo de Ministros en julio, por 242.722 euros. Las dos anteriores encarecieron la actuación en casi 1,9 millones, una de ellas para rediseñar 3,5 kilómetros en la Serra do Careón por motivos ambientales. La obra suma tres décadas y es una de las demoras más largas de la red viaria estatal.

El ministro de Transportes, Óscar Puente, anunció a comienzos de 2025 que la autovía estaría completa a finales de ese año. La promesa no se cumplió, y en septiembre el PPdeG se concentró en Nadela para denunciar un "castigo" del Gobierno central a la provincia de Lugo. La alcaldesa de la ciudad, Elena Candia, reprochó al ministro el incumplimiento de su propio plazo.

Los populares citaron también el estado del firme en la A-6, la parálisis de la A-74 hacia A Mariña y de la A-56 con Ourense, y la falta de mantenimiento en la N-540 y la N-120. Mientras el último enlace siga en obras, el trayecto entre las dos capitales gallegas continúa haciéndose en buena parte por carretera convencional.

articles.headline: La huelga general del 11-N llega con seguimiento incierto y la CEOE en pie de guerra
articles.subtitle: Los sondeos sitúan en torno al 19% quienes secundarán el paro y en el 58% quienes no lo harán, mientras la patronal coordina a sus organizaciones para vigilar la jornada y no descarta acciones legales.
articles.body:
La huelga general convocada para este miércoles llega con el pulso abierto entre los convocantes y la patronal. Un sondeo de Sigma Dos para EL MUNDO, con 4.172 entrevistas entre el 30 de octubre y el 6 de noviembre, sitúa en el 19,1% los que tienen claro que la secundarán, frente al 58% que no la harán y un 6,7% que aún duda pero se inclina por trabajar.

El mismo estudio señala una paradoja: el 42,7% se declara de acuerdo con la convocatoria, pero una parte de ese grupo no piensa movilizarse. Y el 53,7% cree que el llamamiento responde a motivos políticos y busca influir en la campaña del 29-N, frente al 42,7% que lo atribuye a la situación del empleo y de la vivienda.

El origen de la protesta fue la muerte de Maricarmen Abascal, de 87 años, dos semanas después de ser desahuciada de su casa en el distrito madrileño de Retiro. CCOO, UGT y otras organizaciones han llamado a parar, y la CEOE ha movilizado a sus patronales para seguir la jornada sin descartar acciones legales.

Otra encuesta, de 40dB para EL PAÍS, añade dos datos de clima político: el 30% dice que las elecciones no serán limpias y más de la mitad rechaza las acampadas por la vivienda que se han sucedido en varias ciudades, como la de la Puerta del Sol, desalojada la semana pasada. El 70% cree, erróneamente, que España crece menos que Europa.

articles.headline: La caja negra del Iryo revela que su maquinista avisó del riesgo seis minutos después del choque
articles.subtitle: La conductora del tren 6076 pidió a los pasajeros que no bajaran por el cable de la catenaria caído sobre la vía, mientras Sevilla despedía a las víctimas en una misa funeral.
articles.body:
Cuando el tren 6076 de Iryo fue embestido por un AVE de Renfe en la localidad toledana de Urda, su maquinista hizo dos cosas casi al mismo tiempo. A las 8.59 horas avisó al centro de control de que veía el cable de la catenaria caído sobre la vía y, a la vez, pidió a los viajeros que no abandonaran el tren. "¡No salgan del tren!", advirtió, según la caja negra del vehículo y el registro de comunicaciones.

Iryo solicitó entonces a Atocha que cortara la tensión y la circulación en la vía contigua de forma urgente, mientras los responsables del tráfico intentaban tranquilizar a la conductora y que siguiera las instrucciones desde Madrid. El siniestro, una colisión entre dos trenes de alta velocidad que cubrían el trayecto Madrid-Andalucía, ha dejado 69 muertos y más de un centenar de heridos.

Este lunes, la catedral de Sevilla acogió una misa funeral por las víctimas, siete de ellas de la provincia. El arzobispo, José Ángel Saiz Meneses, pidió "esclarecer las causas" del accidente y "asumir las responsabilidades que sean necesarias", y defendió que las familias tienen "derecho a conocer la verdad". El presidente de la Junta, Juanma Moreno, deseó que "nunca más" se repita una tragedia así.

El acto llega en plena crisis del ferrocarril. Tras la dimisión de Óscar Puente y del presidente de Adif, el ministro Carlos Cuerpo ha pedido a los trabajadores que desescalen su indignación y ha prometido una nueva regulación de seguridad en semanas. Los maquinistas han convocado otra jornada de protesta para el jueves, un día después de la huelga general.

articles.headline: Abascal llama «dictador» a Sánchez en su entrevista en La Revuelta
articles.subtitle: El líder de Vox se estrenó en el programa de Broncano con un público elegido por casting, una bandera de Ceuta como regalo y un debate tenso sobre clima, vivienda, inmigración y violencia machista.
articles.body:
Santiago Abascal se sentó este lunes en el plató de La Revuelta, en el Teatro Albéniz, y salió llamando "dictador" a Pedro Sánchez. La entrevista, la más esperada de la campaña en televisión, se celebró ante un público elegido por casting que recibió al líder de Vox con una ovación y gritos de "presidente, presidente", algo insólito en el programa.

Broncano explicó al inicio que había "cierto temor" a que el público habitual dificultase la conversación y el ritmo de la entrevista. Abascal le regaló una bandera de Ceuta como gesto hacia la ciudad autónoma y, a partir de ahí, la charla derivó en un intercambio de posiciones opuestas sobre cambio climático, vivienda, inmigración y violencia contra las mujeres.

El momento más tenso llegó con el clima. Abascal criticó el "fanatismo climático" y la Agenda 2030 por dañar la competitividad; Broncano calificó sus planteamientos de "peligrosos" e "irresponsables" y defendió las evidencias científicas. El líder de Vox respondió preguntando cuándo había negado él el cambio climático y sostuvo que España no puede imponer restricciones mientras China sigue contaminando.

En vivienda reconoció que es uno de los grandes problemas del país, pero culpó al Gobierno, a la inmigración y a las restricciones al suelo, y admitió que deben vigilarse las prácticas especulativas de los fondos. Sobre la ley de violencia de género aseguró que "tiene que ser revisada", y planteó revisar las relaciones con Marruecos, incluida la organización conjunta del Mundial de 2030.

articles.headline: El Supremo deja votar el 29-N a los 189.000 hijos de nacionalizados por la ley de nietos
articles.subtitle: La Sala de lo Contencioso rechaza las cautelares de Vox e Iustitia Europa y alega el «breve lapso temporal» que queda hasta los comicios, después de haber vetado el voto de los descendientes de exiliados.
articles.body:
El Tribunal Supremo ha rechazado suspender el derecho al voto de los 189.000 hijos de personas nacionalizadas al amparo de la ley de nietos, de modo que podrán participar en las elecciones generales del 29 de noviembre. La Sala de lo Contencioso-Administrativo ha denegado las medidas cautelares que habían solicitado Vox e Iustitia Europa.

El fallo llega después de que el mismo tribunal sí suspendiera el voto de los descendientes de exiliados españoles, identificados por el Gobierno a partir de la documentación aportada. En esta ocasión, los magistrados justifican la negativa en el "breve lapso temporal" que queda hasta los comicios del 29-N, un argumento de calendario y no de fondo.

El debate tiene su origen en los datos que el Ejecutivo remitió al Supremo: de las 163.355 personas nacionalizadas por la ley de nietos, solo 901 acreditaron ser descendientes de exiliados. Vox y Iustitia Europa intentaron extender a todo el colectivo la suspensión ya aplicada a esos descendientes, algo que el tribunal ha rechazado.

La ley de nietos, en vigor desde 2022, permite recuperar la nacionalidad a hijos y nietos de españoles que la perdieron por el exilio. Su aplicación ha estado marcada por la saturación de los consulados, sobre todo en América Latina, y por las dudas sobre cuántos solicitantes podían demostrar el vínculo con un exiliado.

articles.headline: El Gobierno pide a la Fiscalía cerrar TikTok y Sánchez no descarta suspenderlo
articles.subtitle: Una investigación española localizó miles de vídeos y perfiles pedófilos en la plataforma. El Ejecutivo reclama su cierre cautelar y estudia medidas mientras Bruselas amenaza con sanciones.
articles.body:
El Gobierno ha pasado de la advertencia a la amenaza regulatoria con TikTok. Después de que una investigación española localizara miles de vídeos y perfiles pedófilos en la plataforma, el Ejecutivo pidió a la Fiscalía el cierre cautelar del servicio para poder investigar, y Pedro Sánchez afirmó este lunes que no descarta "suspender" la aplicación: "Me parece un escándalo".

El siguiente paso depende de la Fiscalía y de la Comisión Europea. Bruselas ya había exigido cambios en el sistema de recomendaciones de la red social para combatir la adicción, y advirtió de que su diseño puede infringir el reglamento europeo de servicios digitales. Cualquier bloqueo nacional tendría que encajar además con ese marco común, que atribuye a la Comisión la competencia sobre las grandes plataformas.

TikTok, por su parte, ha pedido a Maldita.es su investigación para localizar y eliminar los vídeos detectados y sostiene que colabora con las autoridades españolas y europeas.

El asunto ha entrado de lleno en la campaña del 29-N. El PP ha presentado su propio paquete: prohibir las redes sociales a los menores de 14 años, limitar el scroll infinito y obligar a las plataformas a ofrecer un modo de descanso nocturno. El debate sobre la edad mínima digital ha dejado de ser una discusión de expertos.

articles.headline: Three racist attacks in Derry's Waterside may be linked, police say
articles.subtitle: A care worker suffered a suspected broken leg and a woman had her windscreen smashed with a baton. The PSNI is treating Sunday night's incidents as racially motivated hate crimes.
articles.body:
Police in Derry are investigating three assaults and an incident of criminal damage in the Waterside area of the city on Sunday night, and believe the attacks may be linked. All are being treated as racially motivated hate crimes.

The North West Migrants Forum said a 28-year-old male healthcare worker was attacked close to Clooney Terrace as he spoke to a female relative. He suffered a suspected broken tibia. The woman, also a care worker, had her windscreen smashed with a baton. In a separate incident, a man was chased along Bond Street before being beaten.

The man told the forum that he had just crossed at a set of traffic lights when a group of men approached. One called him a racist slur, he said, and asked where he was from. When he answered "Derry", the reply was "it's Londonderry", and the group began punching him. He escaped, but two of them followed him and kicked him again.

The sister of a brother and sister attacked in a further incident said the family had been left deeply shaken. She said the pair were racially abused after she parked her car, that her sister was punched and that a baton was used on the windscreen, sending glass into her mouth. Their brother was then set upon, and she said the attackers "tried to break both his legs".

articles.headline: Russia and Ukraine resume peace talks in Abu Dhabi as US reports 'some flexibility'
articles.subtitle: It is the first trilateral meeting aimed at ending the war since February. Washington says both sides are softening over who would control Ukraine's east after a settlement.
articles.body:
Russian and Ukrainian officials meet in Abu Dhabi on Tuesday for the first trilateral talks aimed at ending the war since February, with US officials saying privately that both sides are showing "a little bit of flexibility" over who would control Ukraine's eastern regions in a postwar settlement.

Jared Kushner, part of the US delegation alongside envoy Steve Witkoff, said the talks would focus on the "postwar security concerns" of both countries. "An important part of this process is encouraging all parties to begin thinking seriously about what comes after the war," he wrote on X. The meeting comes as the fifth anniversary of the full-scale invasion approaches.

The gap remains wide on Donetsk. Moscow wants Kyiv to hand over the parts of the region it still holds, while Ukraine wants the contact line frozen, arguing those areas are vital to its future security. Ukrainian outlets reported that the talks had been unstuck with European participation and that Washington was promising "a big deal".

Separately, Spain and other allies began joint exercises aimed at preparing a possible deployment once peace arrives. The talks follow a Russian strike on a village in Zaporizhzhia last week in which at least 40 people were killed.

articles.headline: Trump says fresh US strikes on Iran are 'highly unlikely'
articles.subtitle: The president says 'Iran militarily is effectively over' and claims 'positive momentum' in negotiations, days after midterm losses his own party blamed on the war.
articles.body:
Donald Trump said on Monday that renewed US attacks on Iran were "highly unlikely", declaring that "Iran militarily is effectively over" and that there was "positive momentum" behind negotiations to end the conflict. "We're just keeping it the status quo," he told reporters at the White House. "And we're doing that really at the behest of countries that are their neighbours."

He added that US forces were "locked and loaded" should circumstances change, and defended not formally ending the war by citing the risk to Gulf allies, suggesting the naval blockade of Iranian ports was making the region safer. Iranian officials have repeatedly expressed doubt about his earlier claims that the conflict was over.

The shift comes after a bruising midterm result for Republicans last week, which senior figures including Vice-President JD Vance blamed on the Iran war. Before the vote Trump said US forces had carried out "minor strikes" on an Iranian island in the Strait of Hormuz; in a 60 Minutes interview aired on Sunday he said he saw no reason to escalate.

A diplomatic track is taking shape. The Guardian reported that Qatar has floated a plan under which the Strait of Hormuz could reopen as part of a package covering nuclear inspections, and El Mundo reported that Beijing is preparing to host a summit between Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin.

articles.headline: Explosion at Turkish steel plant kills at least 16 workers
articles.subtitle: A crane carrying a replacement boiler collapsed at the Habas plant near Izmir and sent material into a furnace. At least five people have been arrested as rescue work continues.
articles.body:
At least 16 people have died and 13 were injured in an explosion at an iron and steel factory near the port city of Izmir in western Turkey, authorities said. All the casualties were workers at the Habas plant, one of the country's leading steel producers. Footage showed a large fire inside the facility and a column of smoke rising over Aliaga.

The local governor said the blast happened around midday when a crane carrying a replacement boiler collapsed, causing material to fall into a furnace below. The company said the accident occurred during scheduled maintenance on one of its electric arc furnaces. Eyewitnesses said the explosion shook the ground, and one person initially believed an earthquake had struck.

Izmir governor Süleyman Elban said some people were believed to still be under the rubble. President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan confirmed the deaths after a cabinet meeting on Monday and said investigations were under way, with two of the injured in a serious condition. At least five people have been arrested, according to local media cited by BBC Turkish.

Reports on the toll varied during the day, with some outlets putting it at 16 and others at 17 by Monday evening. Workplace accidents remain a chronic problem in Turkey, according to the independent Health and Safety Labour Watch.

articles.headline: At least 34 die as migrant boat sinks off Senegal on route to the Canaries
articles.subtitle: One person was rescued and the number missing is unknown. The wooden boat capsized between Dakar and Saint-Louis while heading for Spain's Canary Islands.
articles.body:
At least 34 people have died after a boat carrying migrants sank off the coast of Senegal, the Senegalese Press Agency reported, citing an official source. The interior ministry said one person had been rescued, and that the number of people still missing had yet to be established.

The small wooden boat capsized between the capital, Dakar, and the northern city of Saint-Louis, as it headed towards Spain's Canary Islands. Spanish outlets put the toll at 35 dead with dozens missing, while other reports cited 39, with search operations continuing through Monday night.

Saliou Diouf, founder of the Senegalese migrant aid group Boza Fii, told AFP that all the bodies recovered so far were Senegalese. The nationalities of others on board were yet to be established.

President Bassirou Diomaye Faye expressed condolences and urged young Senegalese not to risk the crossing, pledging to step up the fight against the networks organising the journeys. Walking Borders, a Spanish migrant rights group, recorded 635 deaths on the Atlantic route to the Canaries between January and May 2026 — the highest toll among the routes it monitors.

articles.headline: Republican congressman forces impeachment vote on Hegseth over Iran war powers
articles.subtitle: Thomas Massie says the defence secretary broke the law by waging hostilities in Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorisation. The vote is expected to fail.
articles.body:
Republican congressman Thomas Massie formally introduced articles of impeachment against Defence Secretary Pete Hegseth on the House floor on Monday and plans to force a vote this week, alleging that he has violated the US Constitution.

"By engaging in hostilities in Iran for more than 90 days without congressional authorization, Secretary Hegseth is breaking the law and must be held accountable," Massie said. The effort will most likely fail while Republicans remain in control of Congress until January, but Massie says he wants to push Donald Trump to fire Hegseth before Democrats can launch their own process.

Hegseth, who has not held a news conference since May, said he was not concerned and will hold one on Tuesday morning "on that very topic". The Kentucky congressman, who lost his own re-election bid this year, first introduced impeachment articles in September and is pressing for a vote after Republicans lost both chambers in last week's midterms.

Trump has doubled down in defence of Hegseth and attacked the fresh effort. The push underlines how the Iran war, now nearly nine months old, has become a fault line inside the Republican Party, with Massie among the few willing to criticise the president over it.

articles.headline: Nvidia's spy scandal deepens as Trump confirms an FBI investigation
articles.subtitle: The US president said the bureau is looking into Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy, as shareholder lawyers circle and the chipmaker's shares slide.
articles.body:
Donald Trump said on Monday that the FBI is investigating Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang's relationship with a woman accused of being a Chinese spy, deepening a scandal that has knocked the chipmaker's shares and unsettled the wider AI industry.

Nvidia has confirmed it opened an internal review after the relationship became public. Since then a short seller has said he flagged Huang's ties to the woman six months before the story broke, and US law firms have begun competing to file shareholder suits, according to TechCrunch.

El País reported that the woman, identified as Alice Huang, reached the chief executive through what the paper described as a seduction operation run from China. Beijing has not confirmed that account, and Nvidia has said only that it is reviewing the matter.

The affair lands at a delicate moment. Nvidia is the bellwether of the AI trade, its China business is already constrained by export controls, and its stock has fallen sharply since the story broke. Wired reported that the fallout is being felt across the sector rather than contained to one company, as partners and investors wait to see what the FBI finds.

articles.headline: France blames Iran's Revolutionary Guard for hacking supermarket freezers and blood banks
articles.subtitle: Paris calls the campaign 'unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression' and will push for EU sanctions, after fridges were heated to spoil food worth millions of euros.
articles.body:
France has formally accused Iran of carrying out cyber-attacks on internet-connected refrigeration units across the country and beyond. Foreign minister Jean-Noël Barrot told reporters in Paris on Monday that responsibility lay with the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps, calling the campaign "unprecedented in both its scale and its level of aggression".

In October, hackers remotely raised the temperature of fridges and freezers in hundreds of supermarkets in France, spoiling fresh and frozen food estimated to be worth millions of euros. Last week dozens of supermarkets in seven other European countries were hit in a similar wave; it is not yet known whether the incidents are linked.

Blood banks were also targeted. The French Blood Establishment said the attacks were stopped before any blood was spoiled. Researchers had warned that the web-based controllers managing fleets of industrial chilling units were exposed, and that some of the affected Danfoss models no longer receive security fixes.

Barrot said France would press for European sanctions against those responsible. Separately, the Paris prosecutor opened an investigation into the head of an offensive cyber unit linked to the Revolutionary Guard. Iran has not responded to the allegations.

articles.headline: AI's power bill comes due as CoreWeave yields spike and Anthropic buys $3.4bn of turbines
articles.subtitle: The data-centre landlord's bonds now yield more than 16%, while Anthropic has bought Caterpillar generators capable of 1.7 gigawatts — compute is becoming a credit and energy problem.
articles.body:
Two numbers tell the story of AI's infrastructure squeeze. CoreWeave's bond yield has climbed above 16%, CNBC reported, a level that signals investors are pricing genuine credit risk into the data-centre landlord. And Anthropic has spent $3.4bn on Caterpillar natural gas generators able to produce up to 1.7 gigawatts, according to the Financial Times.

Anthropic, which is preparing to go public, had preferred to rent rather than own its infrastructure: its S-1 filing in May disclosed payments of $1.25bn a month to xAI through May 2029 for computing power. Buying turbines outright looks like a last resort when the backlog for gas turbines stretches into the early 2030s and grid connections can take just as long.

The generators had originally been ordered by equipment supplier OnePWR, which could not secure financing, so Anthropic went straight to the manufacturer. TechCrunch also reported on Monday that the company is moving forward with plans for an initial public offering.

The pressure is visible in public markets. AI stocks have swung sharply since last week's US midterms, with trillions wiped from valuations before a partial rebound, as investors question whether the build-out can ever earn back what it costs.

articles.headline: US regulators question whether Waymo's school-bus software fix actually worked
articles.subtitle: NHTSA has opened a recall query covering 2,895 robotaxis after finding most illegal passings of stopped school buses happened after the update had been installed.
articles.body:
America's road safety regulator has opened a recall query into Waymo, questioning whether the software fix the company issued for its robotaxis actually stopped them passing stopped school buses. The query covers 2,895 vehicles equipped with Waymo's fifth-generation automated driving system, Reuters reported.

NHTSA said it had identified a large number of incidents in which Waymo vehicles passed school buses with red lights flashing or the stop arm extended. Most of them occurred after 17 November 2025, when the software update meant to prevent such violations had been completed across the fleet.

The agency said the query, opened on Friday, would assess the adequacy of the remedy and identify the cause of the continued violations. A recall query is the step regulators take when they suspect a completed recall did not fix the defect.

Waymo says it identified the software issue behind the incidents and that the updates improved its vehicles' performance, and it plans a voluntary software recall. In Austin, Texas, where the problem first surfaced, the school district counted 20 citations in a single school year and asked the company to pause operations while pupils boarded buses; Waymo declined.

articles.headline: Europe's data-centre backlash reaches Spain as operators fight a new decree
articles.subtitle: Protests in 15 countries demanding a moratorium coincide with Spanish operators asking the government to rewrite rules that would tighten control over new facilities.
articles.body:
Spain was one of 15 European countries where protests were called this weekend demanding a moratorium on new data centres, in what El País described as the first coordinated European mobilisation against the industry. Organisers argued that the regions hosting the facilities are being treated as somebody else's backyard.

In Spain the fight is also regulatory. Data-centre operators have asked the minister for ecological transition, Sara Aagesen, to revise the decree that will govern the sector, after the Council of State gave the draft its final procedural clearance before approval, 20minutos reported.

The objections echo those raised elsewhere in Europe: strain on electricity grids, water consumption, land take, and the share of new renewable capacity consumed by computing rather than by households and industry.

In the United States the same dynamic is producing unusual coalitions. Wired reported that bikers and insect enthusiasts have joined forces to oppose a new Google data centre, one of a growing number of local campaigns that cut across conventional politics.

articles.headline: Anthropic ships Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2, and cuts Fable's price
articles.subtitle: The lab says the new models handle 'daunting' engineering work, run 30% faster and now undercut GPT-6 Astra on input tokens. Mythos is limited to vetted organisations.
articles.body:
Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 on Monday, the first models since Fable and Mythos 5.1 in September. The company says both improve on coding, reasoning and vision, respond more clearly, and generate output faster than their predecessors.

Fable 5.2 is available from today; Mythos 5.2 is restricted to vetted organisations. In pre-release testing Anthropic says the models designed three working electronic devices from scratch, made progress on robotics evaluations, solved two open problems in the physics of black holes and formalised the proof of Fermat's Last Theorem in 30 hours, and helped its engineers complete software migrations the company calls otherwise infeasible.

Commercially, the sharper news is price. Anthropic is cutting Fable's cost from $10 to $8 per million input tokens, which puts it below its main competitor, GPT-6 Astra, and it says responses come back 30% faster across effort levels. Faster serving is available at double the price. Fable 5.2 also supports zero data retention through the company's Enterprise Frontier Safeguards, a long-standing sticking point for corporate buyers.

The launch is also Anthropic's first since METR, an outside evaluator, reported that internal models appeared to be speeding up the lab's own research by roughly 2x — the kind of finding that raises the question of recursive self-improvement. METR stressed that many uncertainties remain. Fable 5.2 scores 65 on Artificial Analysis' composite index, the highest recorded so far.

articles.headline: Meta's Muse Ember aims at the unglamorous half of agentic AI: volume
articles.subtitle: At 10 cents per million input tokens, the Superintelligence Lab's lightest model is built to sit under a bigger planner and do the tool calls, routing and extraction.
articles.body:
Meta's Superintelligence Lab released Muse Ember on Monday, describing it as its lightest and most cost-efficient model yet. Ember is built for the repetitive work agents do all day: tool calls, coding subtasks, routing, extraction and parsing long documents.

The pitch is cost per task rather than benchmark bragging. At 10 cents per million input tokens, Meta positions Ember as significantly cheaper than Anthropic's Haiku and OpenAI's Luna while remaining competitive with open-weight rivals such as DeepSeek V4.1 Flash and GLM 5.3 Flash.

Ember is designed to be paired with a larger model rather than used on its own. In a customer-support agent, for instance, a heavier model sets the rules for handling an issue and the lighter one applies them across tens of thousands of cases. Meta's summary is blunt: "Muse Wonder plans, Muse Ember handles the volume."

The strategy mirrors what has happened across the market this year, as the cost of inference became the deciding variable for anyone running agents at scale. Cheaper per-task models make long chains of tool calls affordable, and they make it harder for frontier labs to justify premium pricing on routine work.

articles.headline: Apple starts selling AI by the pack: $49.99 for extra Logic Pro assistant use
articles.subtitle: Logic Pro 13 is the first app with a 'Buy More Usage' button. Packs need a Creator Studio subscription, cannot be shared with family and don't say how much usage they contain.
articles.body:
Apple has begun charging for extra Apple Intelligence usage. Logic Pro 13 is the first app with a "Buy More Usage" option, selling a one-time "intelligence usage pack" for $49.99 in the United States. 9to5Mac spotted the listing on Monday and MacRumors confirmed the US price.

The packs are available only to subscribers of Apple Creator Studio, the $12.99-a-month bundle of creative apps, and only once the monthly limit on the Logic assistant is reached. Apple sells them in eight countries: Brazil, Canada, France, Germany, India, Mexico, the United Kingdom and the United States.

The terms are restrictive. A pack can be used only by the Apple Account that bought it, Family Sharing does not apply, unused usage rolls over month to month but expires 12 months after purchase, and sales are final. Apple does not disclose how much extra usage a pack buys, which makes it hard to compare with simply paying for a subscription.

Apple has said since September that some features would carry usage limits because they call cloud models from OpenAI and Google. The Logic assistant needs an Apple silicon Mac, macOS 27 or later and US English, and the packs are expected to reach Final Cut Pro, Pixelmator Pro and the iWork apps this month.
